scope: Verification status and access limits are per record; inherited codec references are explicitly marked, not freshly re-audited.

references.title: Dolma: Deduplication documentation
authors: Allen Institute for AI / Dolma contributors
references.supports: In-memory Bloom tagging can classify documents or paragraphs as duplicates; mixer subsequently drops them; false positives are acknowledged.
references.limitations: Moving main branch; motivates application only. We did not benchmark Dolma or claim its implementation maintains our exact authoritative log.

references.title: Distinct Sampling for Highly-Accurate Answers to Distinct Values Queries and Event Reports
inspected_passages: Sections 3.1 and 3.2, printed pages 544 onward / PDF page 4
references.supports: Occurrence sampling favors frequent values; hash-consistent sampling can sample distinct IDs with bounded storage. Our bottom-k baseline belongs to this established family.
references.limitations: Its level-based implementation and query-estimation objective differ from our simple bottom-k auditing use; no claim of identical end-to-end application.

references.title: Mitigating False Positives in Filters: To Adapt or to Cache?
references.venue: ACM Transactions on Database Systems 51(3), Article 17
inspected_passages: Indexed primary publisher abstract, metadata, and Introduction
references.supports: Direct modern predecessor for adaptation versus caching under Zipfian and network workloads; explicitly requires an oracle identifying false positives.
references.limitations: Direct open returned an internal error on one attempt; primary publisher indexed text supplied abstract and complete visible introduction. Detailed algorithm limitation is additionally supported by the accessible 2021 full text.

references.title: Mitigating False Positives in Filters: to Adapt or to Cache?
inspected_passages: Introduction page 2 on serendipitous false-positive corrections
references.supports: Broom fingerprint repair can eliminate other future false positives; backing dictionary supplies a colliding stored element, whose access is accounted for asymptotically in that setting.
references.limitations: Not implemented here. Ordinary-Bloom idempotence and min(B,U) scoped oracle bounds do not cover collateral corrections from these adaptive representations.

references.title: Approximately Detecting Duplicates for Streaming Data using Stable Bloom Filters
inspected_passages: Introduction and URL crawling motivating example, PDF page 1
references.supports: Approximate stream deduplication and the possibility of missed new URLs under limited resources are established applications; stable filters evict old information.
references.limitations: Not the same model: our exact processed log persists and our insert-only Bloom does not evict entries. No quantitative SBF guarantee was reused.

references.title: Minimizing Regret With Label Efficient Prediction
inspected_passages: Sections I and II, PDF pages 1–2
references.supports: Learning from a bounded number of paid outcome observations is an established problem with regret bounds.
references.limitations: Adjacent prior art, not a theorem directly subsuming mutable deduplication: processing changes future membership labels and our loss counts distinct retained documents.

references.title: LSHBloom: Internet-Scale Text Deduplication
references.supports: Current probabilistic document-deduplication research evaluates memory/runtime/accuracy and configurable Bloom false-positive overhead. A generic Bloom-for-corpus use is not a novelty claim.
references.limitations: Near-duplicate LSH problem differs from our exact-ID audit allocation. HTML title differs from arXiv metadata title; placeholder PVLDB DOI in source does not establish publication. We did not validate all of its mathematical claims.

references.title: Honey Encryption: Security Beyond the Brute-Force Bound
references.examined: Author publication page; full-text Section 4 (DTE and inverse sampling).
references.relationship: Direct predecessor for abstract codec distribution shaping and randomized within-fiber encoding; different cryptographic object.
references.scope_for_this_candidate: DTE marginal shaping does not supply a joint frozen-table guarantee. Inherited verification; not re-audited here.

references.title: Probability Model Transforming Encoders Against Encoding Attacks
references.relationship: Encoding-attack and probability-model precedent; not claimed to solve the same retrieval optimization.
references.scope_for_this_candidate: Encoding-attack precedent from the completed codec audit, not asserted to contain this occupancy attack. Inherited verification.

references.title: Adversarial Correctness and Privacy for Probabilistic Data Structures
references.examined: Author preprint metadata, abstract and introductory security-model discussion; abstract says accepted CCS 2022.
references.relationship: API/internal-state and adaptive privacy framework for AMQ; membership rather than identical retrieval-value problem.
references.scope_for_this_candidate: Re-read primary full text Section 5 and Theorems 5.4/5.6: snapshot/adaptive whole-view privacy, with permitted leakage explicit.

references.title: Ribbon: Fast Succinct Static Retrieval and Approximate Membership
references.examined: Publisher PDF deposited by authors' institution; Section 1.7 and Section 5.4 Lemma 5.4.

references.scope_for_this_candidate: Reopened current publisher PDF metadata; row-span Lemma 5.4 was verified in previous audit. Not a general multi-query privacy theorem.

references.scope_for_this_candidate: Re-read full-text Definitions 3/4, Algorithm 1, and double-obliviousness proof; uniformly random values are an explicit assumption.
